key_insight: Fusing features from multiple network levels creates representations that are both stable and adaptable, enabling efficient continual learning for changing visual quality inspection tasks.
problem_solved: Enables deployed vision models in volatile manufacturing/remanufacturing settings to adapt quickly to new products and defect patterns without costly full retraining or severe forgetting of prior knowledge.
method: Introduce a multi-level feature fusion module that combines low-, mid- and high-level features to form robust, adaptable representations.
Use the fused representations within a continual learning pipeline to balance plasticity (learning new defects) and stability (retaining prior knowledge).
Optimize for computationally efficient incremental updates so models can be adapted on-device or with limited compute resources.
impact: Allows AI/ML practitioners in manufacturing to maintain high inspection performance across evolving conditions while keeping adaptation time and compute low — reducing downtime and labeling effort in production settings.
visual_elements: Layered network schematic showing low/mid/high-level feature maps feeding into a fusion block (illustrates where fusion occurs).
Timeline or stream diagram of continual learning: new tasks arrive → quick fusion-based update → preserved previous performance (visualize low forgetting).
Bar/line chart comparing adaptation speed and retained accuracy vs baseline continual-learning approaches.
Example inspection image grid showing original defects, post-adaptation detection results, and failure cases handled by fusion.
paper_title: Multi-Level Feature Fusion for Continual Learning in Visual Quality Inspection
paper_authors: Johannes C. Bauer, Paul Geng, Stephan Trattnig, Petr Dokládal, Rüdiger Daub
